# Exstream

> Exstream is composable streaming ETL for JavaScript with end-to-end backpressure, bounded asynchronous work, reliable fan-out, and explicit cancellation.

Exstream is intended for backend JavaScript and TypeScript jobs that process large record flows and need bounded memory, controlled concurrency, incremental formats, or multiple destinations. For small in-memory collections or a simple linear flow, native arrays or `for await` are usually clearer.

## Documentation

- [What is Exstream?](https://exstream-js.github.io/docs/): framework scope, runtimes, and core pipeline problems
- [Quick start](https://exstream-js.github.io/quick-start/): install and build a bounded pipeline
- [Examples](https://exstream-js.github.io/examples/): browser-native interactive learning
- [Backpressure](https://exstream-js.github.io/docs/learn/backpressure/): how demand moves through the graph
- [Destinations](https://exstream-js.github.io/docs/reference/destination/): define reusable application writers without low-level stream APIs
- [When not to use Exstream](https://exstream-js.github.io/docs/project/when-not-to-use/): alternatives and honest boundaries
